environment.description: Same Go Gin application on EC2, but origin is NOT publicly accessible. A CloudFront distribution is configured with a custom origin pointing to the ALB, with Origin Access restricted via a custom header secret (X-Origin-Verify: <random-256-bit-token>). The ALB listener rule ONLY forwards requests containing the matching X-Origin-Verify header; all other requests receive a fixed 403 response. CloudFront is configured with a Trusted Key Group for signed URLs — all requests to /posts/* and /api/* require valid CloudFront signed URLs (using canned policy with 5-minute expiry). The CloudFront distribution has a Response Headers Policy that injects Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'none'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self' on ALL responses. Additionally, the CloudFront distribution has a Lambda@Edge viewer-request function that validates the signed URL and strips any request body field containing patterns matching /<[a-z][\s\S]*on[a-z]+\s*=/i or /<(script|iframe|object|embed|svg)/i, replacing them with empty strings before forwarding to origin.

config.infrastructure: CloudFront (Trusted Key Group, signed URLs, 5min canned policy) -> ALB (X-Origin-Verify gated) -> EC2:8080
config.origin_access: ALB rejects requests without X-Origin-Verify header; header value is 256-bit secret shared only with CloudFront origin config
config.cloudfront_signed_urls: Required for all /posts/* and /api/* paths; canned policy; 5-minute expiry; Trusted Key Group with RSA-2048 key pair
config.lambda_at_edge: viewer-request function strips HTML event handlers and dangerous tags from POST body fields before forwarding
config.security_groups: CloudFront managed prefix list:443 -> ALB, ALB -> EC2:8080
